tunnel.title: Connections

onboarding.title: Welcome to UnifiedEnv Easy Gateway
onboarding.subtitle: Follow these steps to set up your first connection.
onboarding.step1Desc: Configure the server you want to connect through — address, user, and key.
onboarding.step2Desc: Choose the connection type, bind port, and target. Pick the Host you just created.
onboarding.step3Desc: Start the connection and verify the connection status from this dashboard.

form.localPortTooltip: Port on your local machine that listens for connections and forwards them through the server.
form.remotePortTooltip: Port on the remote server that listens for connections and forwards them back to your local network.
form.dynamicPortTooltip: Port on your local machine that acts as a SOCKS5 proxy.
form.localTargetHostTooltip: The destination reachable from the server side. Typically an internal IP or hostname inside the remote network.
form.remoteTargetHostTooltip: The destination reachable from your local machine. Typically localhost or a local network address.
form.bindExternalTooltip: If checked, the connection listens on all network interfaces (0.0.0.0) so other devices on the same network can connect. Otherwise it only accepts connections from this machine.
form.noHostDesc: Please create a Host first before creating a connection.

tunnel.typeTooltip: Forward: forwards a port from your machine through the server to a remote target. Example: access a database on the server-side private network. Reverse: forwards a port from the remote server back to your local machine. Example: expose a local dev server to the remote server. SOCKS5 Proxy: creates a SOCKS proxy through the server. Use it as a proxy in your browser or other apps. HTTP→SOCKS5 Proxy: converts an HTTP proxy into a SOCKS5 proxy with optional domain-based routing rules.

host.title: Hosts

form.nameTooltip: A server that your connections connect through. Create it once and reuse it across multiple connections.
form.addressTooltip: Format: user{'@'}host:port. Example: root{'@'}192.168.1.1:22. Port defaults to 22 if omitted.

host.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this host?
host.inUse: Host is in use by a connection and cannot be deleted.

key.title: Keys
key.tooltip: Copy the public key and add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the target server for the user you intend to connect as. This avoids sending passwords over the network and is more secure than password login.
key.inUse: Key is in use by a host and cannot be deleted.
